content:
According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the progress of promoting ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, believing its performance is "far below expectations," a situation that began to emerge after its 2024 launch. Details are as follows.

OpenAI is asking the court to rule before trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk said that X, which has been merged into SpaceXAI, will sue Apple and OpenAI over allegations of alleged collusion to suppress competitors in the artificial intelligence industry. The lawsuit stems from OpenAI's agreement with Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

After the case was formally filed, the scope of the lawsuit has in fact gone beyond the App Store ranking issues Musk publicly complained about. X and SpaceXAI also accuse Apple of attempting to suppress the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to build an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, the companies involved submitted briefs, accusations, and rebuttals to the court. Apple and OpenAI have repeatedly argued that the agreement is not the exclusive partnership alleged in the lawsuit; court documents filed during the same period have also revealed new details about how the two sides' collaboration operates.

One of these details was disclosed in a document OpenAI filed today. According to the Financial Times, OpenAI "expressed disappointment at iPhone users' low interest in the 'Apple Intelligence' ChatGPT feature," a situation that emerged after the agreement was reached in 2024.

The report pointed out:

Court documents made public on Wednesday show that when the agreement was reached in 2024, OpenAI had originally expected that its promotional and branding collaboration with Apple would produce a "halo effect" and anticipated gaining more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, within a month of the ChatGPT integration feature's launch, its performance had a "slow start," and OpenAI immediately revised downward its weekly active user growth forecast. The documents state that by the summer of 2025, "it had become clearly evident that Apple's integration performance for ChatGPT was significantly far below expectations."

The report pointed out that several passages of conversation in the documents filed today were redacted, but the unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives were concerned that Apple might "want to move faster" to find another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Federighi said in an interview that the company ultimately wanted to let users choose between different AI models, specifically mentioning that Google Gemini could potentially be one of the integration options in the future.

That particular partnership ultimately failed to materialize, but Apple later adopted Google's Gemini model to power the new Siri AI; Xcode has also expanded support for Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI's coding agent tools.

Returning to today's documents, the Financial Times mentioned that the documents also pointed out that Apple's implementation of ChatGPT may be one of the reasons for low adoption, because the relevant integration feature is off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recent securities disclosure filings undermine SpaceXAI's claim that its collaboration with Apple harms competition. OpenAI stated in the documents that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is filled with disclosures that are "completely opposite" to the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit.

Based on all of the above, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favor on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before trial. The case is currently scheduled to be heard in January.

Readers can find related coverage in the Financial Times and Reuters reports.
